issues: Dolphin body is filled with heavy random dither/noise dots instead of a smooth lit phosphor form, making it read as a grainy pointillist cloud rather than a glowing OEL object.
The pectoral fin / lower belly renders as a separate blob detached from the main body by a dark gap, breaking the silhouette into two pieces.
Dolphin sits too high in the frame, leaving a dark void in the center-right and failing to gracefully fill the middle 50-60% of display height.
Tail fluke is indistinct and merges into the body noise, weakening the leaping-dolphin read.
Bottom-left VU meter blocks are comparatively bright and pull the eye away from the dolphin.
Phosphor hue reads cyan/teal rather than the characteristic deep blue or green of a 1998-2003 Pioneer OEL panel.
suggestions: Replace the random interior dither with a solid or smoothly-graded phosphor body plus a single crisp rim-light edge, so the dolphin looks like a lit object, not stipple noise.
Bridge the pectoral fin to the torso so the silhouette is one continuous creature with no dark seam.
Scale and recenter the dolphin so its arc spans more width and occupies the middle 50-60% of height, eliminating the empty center-right region.
Sharpen the dorsal fin and tail fluke outlines so the anatomy reads cleanly at 320x128.
Add a short, low-alpha persistence trail behind the dolphin to convey leap motion and authentic OEL phosphor decay without fogging the scene.
Dim the bottom-left VU segments a notch and keep the FFT bar row low-contrast so neither competes with the centerpiece.
Shift the palette toward authentic blue or green phosphor and add a faint scanline/vignette texture for period-correct CRT-OEL character.
